summary.name: Proxyman
summary.one_liner: Proxyman is a native HTTP/HTTPS debugging proxy app for macOS (with iOS, Android, and other platforms mentioned) that captures, decrypts, inspects, and mocks web traffic.
use_cases: Debugging API requests and responses from Mac apps
Mocking backend responses with local files
Inspecting WebSocket messages in real time
Capturing traffic from iOS and Android devices and simulators
Letting an AI agent analyze captured traffic via MCP
summary.what_it_does: Proxyman captures HTTP and HTTPS traffic between apps and servers, decrypting it so requests and responses can be read in plain text. It offers filters (wildcard, regex, multiple, saved), full-text search, and per-app or per-domain views. Breakpoint, Map Local, Map Remote, and a JavaScript scripting tool let users modify or mock requests and responses without changing client code. The app also includes WebSocket and HTTP/2 inspection, a GraphQL matching rule, a diff tool, and a compose-request feature with cURL import. An MCP server lets AI assistants such as Claude Code fetch flows and create debugging rules from the terminal.
notable: Native macOS app with MCP server integration for AI agents
Map Local, Breakpoint, and JavaScript scripting for modifying traffic
Automatic setup for iOS Simulator, Android emulators, and scripted terminals
caveats: Some features are marked PRO (e.g., Two Panes, Network Extension transparent proxy), and the page mentions a Lifetime deal for the offline macOS app
Transparent proxy feature is in BETA and requires macOS 26+
Team Workspace features are presented as a separate offering; pricing details are not given on the page
